stories.headline: CPI leader Binoy Viswam demands Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged BJP ties
stories.title: CPI leader Binoy Viswam demands Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged BJP ties
stories.summary: This comes after former Kerala Chief Secretary Jiji Thomson claimed that Gyanesh Kumar urged him to contest Parliamentary elections on a BJP ticket in 2016.
reasons: source: event has 3 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 3 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar’s total subservience to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has been exposed fully, following the startling revelation by the former Chief Secretary, Jiji Thomson, the State secretary of CPI, Binoy Viswam has said.

Mr. Thomson had earlier alleged that during his tenure as the Chief Secretary, Mr. Kumar had once asked him why he did not contest Parliamentary elections on a BJP ticket, saying he could have become a Union Minister.
According to Mr. Thomson, the conversation had happened in 2016, while the two were travelling on the same flight to New Delhi.

In a statement here, Mr. Viswam said that by offering the lure of a Union Minister’s post under the BJP to a senior civil servant in Keralam, Mr. Kumar has proved that he is someone who is willing to stoop to any level for the BJP.
He said Mr. Kumar later headed the infamous Ayodhya Trust and that the BJP is using the same person to crush democracy for Amit Shah, Mr. Viswam added.
He alleged that Mr. Kumar had been made the CEC as a reward for all the intrigues he has carried out on behalf of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Shah.
Mr. Kumar’s conduct has now become unacceptable even to the other Election Commissioners, he stated.
Mr. Kumar has robbed 13 crore Indians of their right to vote and is a disgrace to the world’s largest democracy.
All democratic-minded Indians now believe that elections can never be free and fair under such an individual, Mr. Viswam claimed.
He demanded that Mr. Kumar should resign from the CEC post immediately if he retained even a shred of loyalty to the Constitution or that he would have to surrender before mounting public fury.
Mr. Viswam added that after Mr. Kumar’s exit, the Electronic Voting Machines too need to exit Indian democracy.

stories.headline: Election Commission on SIR row: Agendas to be shared before meetings, minutes to follow
stories.title: Election Commission on SIR row: Agendas to be shared before meetings, minutes to follow
stories.summary: The Commission maintained that its decisions relating to the SIR exercise were taken with the approval of all three Election Commissioners
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Saturday announced new measures to bring greater procedural transparency to its functioning amid the ongoing controversy over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The poll panel said agendas for all Commission meetings will now be circulated in advance, while minutes of the meetings will be issued after deliberations.
The decision came at a meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Nirvachan Sadan in New Delhi, attended by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

The meeting followed reports alleging that Sandhu and Joshi had raised objections on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months regarding aspects of the SIR exercise and the functioning of the poll panel.
Addressing the controversy, the ECI said the June 24, 2025 order for conducting SIR across all states and Union Territories was approved unanimously by all three commissioners.
The Commission also said the SIR schedules issued subsequently for 12 States/UTs and another 19 States/UTs received unanimous approval.
The poll panel further stated that differences in views and observations are part of institutional deliberations and maintained that its orders have legal sanction and follow statutory procedures.

The ECI also clarified that letters sent by Sandhu and Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary concerned the functioning of an officer deputed to the Commission and were not related to any policy matter or the functioning of its.
IT division.
The SIR exercise has emerged as one of the largest electoral-roll revision exercises in recent years.

According to reports, more than 13 crore names were struck off draft electoral rolls across 30 States and Union Territories during the exercise, intensifying scrutiny over the process of additions, deletions and voter verification.

In Delhi, the Supreme Court recently questioned the manner in which notices were issued to voters, with more than 33 lakh voters receiving notices over issues including alleged “logical discrepancies”.

stories.headline: Election Commission’s bid at damage control raises more questions
stories.title: Election Commission’s bid at damage control raises more questions
stories.summary: The Election Commission’s bid to project unity may have backfired: after all the three Commissioners met, its statement appeared to acknowledge lapses flagged by The Indian Express.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: - All three Election Commissioners met on 26 September amid criticism of the Commission’s handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
- A press note issued after the meeting announced changes to meeting procedures, voter-registration requirements and the handling of some SIR cases.
- The measures address several issues raised in The Indian Express investigation, but questions remain about how earlier decisions were made.
The jury is out on whether the Election Commission of India on Saturday climbed out of the hole it dug for itself since June, 2025 or it merely succeeded in digging the hole deeper.

As protests spread across the country for removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, scrapping the contentious Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and an independent inquiry into the Commission’s functioning, all three Commissioners met at 3 pm on Saturday and tried to reassure people that all is well.
All is not well though.

Even as the Election Commission met today, a damning claim was made by a former Chief secretary of Kerala, Jiji Thomson, who claimed to Manorama Online that Gyanesh Kumar in 2016 had asked him to contest on a BJP ticket.
While Kumar was appointed an Election Commissioner in March, 2024 and became the Chief Election Commissioner in February, 2025, the damning claim reveals his close association with the ruling party.
It would make his position more untenable and make it more difficult for him to remain in his post.

The bland press note issued by the ECI, being described as too little and coming too late, showed both desperation and a desperate attempt to repair the damage done to the Commission’s image and credibility.

The press note issued today, 26 September 2026, does no deny any of the points raised in the Indian Express report and by two of the Election Commissioners on 14 different occasions in the last 10 months, as reported by the Express and others.
The press note in fact accepts that no agenda was being circulated before the meetings of the Commission and no minutes afterwards.
